title: The Open Monsoon
premise: When an unprecedented low tide exposes a sea cave on the Khoral coast, disgraced mountain guide Wendell Eriksen finds a dead man's journal mapping a high pass that opens only before the dry season ends—and evidence that the cave's legendary 'toll' was actually a smuggled inheritance stolen from a village wiped off official maps. Pursued by the magistrate who blacklisted him and shadowed by the dead man's daughter, Wendell must lead an unlikely party across the range ahead of the snows to return what was taken and expose the ledger of bribes that erased a whole community. He reaches the pass as the first snow falls, delivers the inheritance and the truth, and chooses exile on his own terms rather than the pardon offered in exchange for silence.
about_author: Wren Coldharbour is the pen name of a former expedition cook who has crossed four major ranges and never once been paid on time. They write adventure fiction from a converted fishing trawler, insisting that all good stories are measured in miles.

chapters.title: The Tide That Lied
chapters.summary: Wendell Eriksen, scraping a living guiding tourists on the Khoral coast, witnesses a once-in-a-decade low tide reveal a cave mouth locals refuse to name. His POV establishes his exile, his rule against curiosity, and the moment he breaks it. Emotional beat: restless guilt disguised as pragmatism.

chapters.title: Admission Charged
chapters.summary: Inside the cave, Wendell finds a skeleton, a weatherproof journal, and a brass strongbox fused shut by salt. The journal belongs to Aldous Vane, a surveyor who vanished eleven years ago. Wendell's POV; the beat is temptation—the box could buy a new life, or end this one.

chapters.title: The Blacklist
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: how Wendell's testimony about a guided party's deaths got twisted into negligence, earning bans from two countries and the enmity of Magistrate Corven Hale. Wendell's POV. Beat: understanding why invisibility became his religion.

chapters.title: A Daughter of Ledger Paper
chapters.summary: Isolde Vane arrives in town asking after her father, carrying letters that match the journal's handwriting. She corners Wendell at the ferry office. Alternating POVs begin. Beat: two liars recognizing each other's craft.

chapters.title: What the Village Paid
chapters.summary: Deciphering Vane's journal reveals the truth: the cave's 'legendary toll' was a smuggling route for the inheritance of Merrow's Reach, a village condemned and erased from maps after Hale's family acquired its deeds. Isolde's POV. Beat: grief sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: Hale Sends Regards
chapters.summary: Magistrate Hale's men search Wendell's cabin; he escapes with the journal but loses the strongbox's location notes. First blood—a dockhand who warned him is beaten. Wendell's POV. Beat: the cost of being seen.

chapters.title: The Dry Season Clock
chapters.summary: An old shepherd explains the window: the high pass, the Saddle of Ashes, closes with the first snows—roughly five weeks out. Wendell calculates routes while Isolde negotiates supplies. Dual POV. Beat: hope arriving with a deadline attached.

chapters.title: Company of the Condemned
chapters.summary: They gather their party: Tam, a teenage runaway who can read stars; Brakka, an exiled engineer; and Sister Ondine, who tends the forgotten graves of Merrow's Reach. Isolde's POV. Beat: a found family forming around a shared grievance.

chapters.title: The Tollgate Town
chapters.summary: At the last settlement before the mountains, Hale's warrant catches up. Wendell talks them past a checkpoint by posing as a burial party for Ondine. Wendell's POV. Beat: his old shame repurposed as skill—he lies like a guide now.

chapters.title: First Ascent, First Betrayal
chapters.summary: Brakka is revealed to have sold word of their route to a Hale informant—not for money, but a pardon for his own crimes. They spare him and cut him loose. Isolde's POV. Beat: trust tested and rationed.

chapters.title: The River That Remembers
chapters.summary: Crossing a glacial river, they find ruins of the old Merrow road the maps pretend never existed—Vane's survey markers still standing. Ondine reads names carved in stone. Wendell's POV. Beat: the past refusing to stay buried.

chapters.title: Storm Above the Treeline
chapters.summary: An early storm pins them in a bivouac; Tam develops altitude sickness. Wendell must choose between speed and safety, echoing the decision that ruined him years ago. Wendell's POV. Beat: facing his defining wound head-on.

chapters.title: What Wendell Did
chapters.summary: Trapped through the night, Wendell finally tells Isolde the full truth of the disaster that blacklisted him: he obeyed orders instead of his own judgment, and people died. Isolde's POV. Beat: confession as the price of leadership.

chapters.title: The Informant's Trail
chapters.summary: Brakka's tip lets Hale's riders enter the mountains behind them. A running skirmish on scree costs them half their supplies. Tam's POV (first time). Beat: the stakes turn mortal and personal.

chapters.title: Ondine's Ground
chapters.summary: Sister Ondine stays behind at a shrine to slow the pursuers, arming herself only with the names of the dead and a magistrate's fear of witnesses. Her POV. Beat: quiet courage as a weapon.

chapters.title: The Saddle of Ashes
chapters.summary: They reach the pass at dusk and find Vane's final cache: the strongbox key and his confession naming every official who profited from Merrow's Reach—including Hale's signature. Wendell's POV. Beat: triumph shadowed by exhaustion and dread.

chapters.title: Snowline
chapters.summary: The snows arrive early. Descending the far side becomes a survival ordeal; Tam worsens, and Brakka reappears, redeeming himself by hauling the boy through whiteout. Isolde's POV. Beat: grace from an unexpected quarter.

chapters.title: Hale at the Pass
chapters.summary: Hale and his riders catch them at the descent, demanding the confession in exchange for pardons and medical help for Tam. Wendell must bargain with the man who destroyed him. Wendell's POV. Beat: power offering corruption dressed as mercy.

chapters.title: The Reading
chapters.summary: Instead of surrendering the document, Wendell reads Vane's confession aloud before Hale's own men—many of whom are sons of Merrow's Reach families. The riders waver. Isolde's POV. Climax begins: justice spoken outside any courtroom.

chapters.title: Judgment of the Range
chapters.summary: Hale attempts to seize the box by force; an avalanche, loosened by the storm, buries his riders and spares the party. Hale survives, stripped of authority when his own men walk away. Wendell's POV. Climax: nature and conscience ruling together.

chapters.title: Merrow's Reach, Restored
chapters.summary: In the valley below, the inheritance funds the rebuilding of the village and memorials for its dead; Tam recovers; Ondine's grave-registry becomes the legal basis for land claims. Isolde's POV. Beat: restitution without erasure.

chapters.title: Miles, Not Years
chapters.summary: Hale offers Wendell a formal pardon if he signs a statement softening the confession. Wendell declines, keeps his blacklist, and walks north with new papers under a name he chose himself. Final beat: freedom measured in miles, on his own terms.
